documents.title: Hip Pain
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called. R hip has been aching for a few weeks, steady dull pain, worse to walk on, back to using the cane indoors. Thinks he's had some low fevers in the evenings and woke up sweaty a couple of nights. No fall or injury. Incision itself looks fine to him, no redness or drainage.

Discussed with PCP: needs to be seen by his orthopedic surgeon promptly - concern for a problem with the new joint. Pt called ortho while on hold with us, appt next Wed 1/25. Advised ED if fever over 101, shaking chills, or the hip becomes red or swollen. Pt agrees.

documents.title: Orthopedic Surgery Clinic Note
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY GROUP - CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 01/25/2023

Reason: right hip pain, low-grade fevers, s/p right THA 09/27/2022.

History: Mr. Graves is about four months out from his right total hip. He did well at first but over the past several weeks has developed a constant, dull ache in the right hip that now limits how far he can walk. He has had low-grade temperatures and some night sweats. He denies any fall or injury. His PCP saw him in November for warfarin monitoring of his mechanical mitral valve, at which time the hip was improving.

PMH: mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, HTN, DM2, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, chronic constipation, history of colon polyps.
Meds: warfarin, lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, aspirin 81.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Afebrile in clinic. Right hip incision well healed. The skin over the hip is not red or warm. Tender to palpation around the prosthesis. ROM limited by pain in all planes. Distal neurovascular exam intact.

X-rays right hip: components in good position, no fracture, no dislocation.

Labs today: WBC 9.0, ESR 55, CRP 25 mg/L. Blood cultures drawn - no growth so far.

Procedure: Right hip aspiration under sterile technique. Synovial fluid: WBC 3,500/uL, 65% neutrophils. Gram stain - no organisms. Culture sent.

Assessment: Right hip pain with elevated inflammatory markers and an abnormal synovial cell count four months after arthroplasty - chronic periprosthetic joint infection until proven otherwise. Await culture.

Plan: We will call with the culture. Likely a staged revision. Infectious disease referral to follow. Will coordinate warfarin management with his PCP.

cc: Primary care physician

events.reason: Orthopedic note: hip aspirate culture result and plan

documents.title: Orthopedic Surgery - Culture Result and Plan
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY GROUP - TELEPHONE NOTE

Right hip aspirate culture from 01/25: Staphylococcus epidermidis, oxacillin-resistant, vancomycin-susceptible. Blood cultures no growth.

Discussed with patient by phone. This confirms a chronic infection of the right total hip. Recommended two-stage exchange: first stage removal of the implant and placement of an antibiotic cement spacer, then 6 weeks of IV antibiotics, then reimplantation once infection markers settle. Patient agrees. Referred to infectious disease. Stage 1 tentatively 02/14. PCP to manage warfarin bridging.

Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: Chronic prosthetic joint infection, right hip

documents.title: Infectious Disease Consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
INFECTIOUS DISEASE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 02/03/2023
Referred by: orthopedic surgery

72M with mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, DM2, CKD 3a, right THA 9/2022, now with chronic PJI of the right hip. Aspirate 1/25 grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, oxacillin-resistant, vancomycin-susceptible. Blood cultures negative. No murmur of concern on my exam beyond his prosthetic valve sounds; given negative blood cultures and no embolic signs I don't think he needs an echo for endocarditis at this time.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 37.2. Well-appearing. Mechanical click. Right hip tender, no sinus tract.

Impression: Chronic periprosthetic infection of the right hip due to methicillin-resistant S. epidermidis.

Recommendations:
1. Agree with two-stage exchange.
2. After stage 1, IV vancomycin dosed by pharmacy to trough 15-20, anticipate 1,250 mg q24h given his kidney function, for 6 weeks from the date of surgery via PICC with home infusion.
3. Weekly CBC, BMP and vancomycin trough while on therapy; copies to PCP, who manages his INR.
4. Off antibiotics at least 2 weeks before reimplantation, with ESR/CRP before stage 2.
5. Follow up in ID clinic at end of therapy.

documents.title: Pre-operative Visit - Hip Revision Stage 1
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here before stage 1 of the R hip revision (implant out, spacer in) on 2/14. Ortho and ID notes reviewed - S. epidermidis, MRSE, plan 6 wks IV vanc after surgery.

He is frustrated but taking it in stride. Hip aches, walking with the cane. Some evening sweats still. No chest pain, SOB, syncope. No bleeding.

Exam: regular, mechanical click crisp. Lungs clear. R hip tender laterally, no redness.

Plan for warfarin, same as September, which went smoothly:
- Last warfarin Wed 2/8.
- Enoxaparin 80 mg q12h starting Fri 2/10, last dose AM 2/13.
- Post-op: warfarin restarts when surgeon allows, heparin in hospital, enoxaparin at home until INR >= 2.5.
- During IV vancomycin the home infusion labs will include INR - we'll get copies and dose from those.
- Watch kidney function on vanc; metformin is fine as long as creatinine holds. Hold metformin day of surgery.

Cleared from a medical standpoint for an elevated-risk procedure.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Right Hip Resection and Antibiotic Spacer
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 02/14/2023  Discharge 02/18/2023

Diagnosis: Chronic periprosthetic joint infection, right total hip (Staphylococcus epidermidis, oxacillin-resistant).
Procedure 02/14/2023: Removal of right total hip components, debridement, placement of an antibiotic-loaded cement spacer. PICC placed 02/16.

Operative cultures: Staphylococcus epidermidis, same susceptibilities as the aspirate.

Course: Uncomplicated. Heparin infusion started POD1 and warfarin restarted the same evening; enoxaparin 80 mg q12h resumed at discharge per PCP plan, until INR >= 2.5. IV vancomycin started post-op and dosed by pharmacy. Creatinine stable. Toe-touch weight bearing with walker.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge meds: home medications unchanged (warfarin 5 mg, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5, aspirin 81). Vancomycin 1,250 mg IV q24h via PICC through 03/28/2023. Enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h until INR >= 2.5.

Disposition: home with home infusion nursing and home PT.
Follow-up: ID clinic at end of therapy, orthopedics 2 weeks, PCP/INR per home infusion labs.

documents.title: Home Infusion Labs - INR
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home infusion labs received. INR now in goal - per PCP stop enoxaparin, continue warfarin 5 mg nightly. Vanc trough and kidney function reviewed by ID pharmacy; creatinine at his baseline. Spoke with pt, he'll tell the home nurse no more injections. INR with next weekly draw.

documents.title: Home Infusion Labs Reviewed
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Weekly home infusion labs in. INR reviewed with PCP, no change - warfarin 5 mg nightly. Kidney function stable on vanc. One more week of IV antibiotics, PICC out after the last dose per ID. Left message for pt with the plan; he called back and confirmed.

events.reason: End of IV therapy, right hip periprosthetic infection

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 03/30/2023

Completed 6 weeks of IV vancomycin on 03/28 for MRSE periprosthetic infection of the right hip (spacer in place since 02/14). Tolerated well; troughs 14.8-16.2 and creatinine stable throughout. PICC removed 03/28, site clean.

Feels better, no fevers or sweats since early in the course. Hip discomfort much less.

Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: afebrile, spacer incision healed, no drainage or erythema.
Labs today: ESR 31, CRP 8 mg/L - down from 55 and 25.

Plan: no antibiotics now (antibiotic holiday). Repeat ESR/CRP in about 4 weeks; if trending down, orthopedics can proceed with reimplantation. Send operative cultures at stage 2. Return as needed.

documents.title: ESR/CRP Before Reimplantation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ESR 24, CRP 4 - continuing to come down off antibiotics. Forwarded to ortho and ID. INR fine, no change. Pt notified via portal; stage 2 date is 5/16.

documents.title: Pre-operative Visit - Hip Reimplantation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op for stage 2 (new R hip prosthesis) 5/16.

Off antibiotics since 3/28. No fevers, no sweats. Getting around with walker/cane on the spacer, mostly sitting more than he'd like. Markers down (ESR 24, CRP 4 last week). No chest pain or SOB, no bleeding.

Exam: afebrile. Regular rhythm with mechanical click. Lungs clear. R hip incision healed.

A/P:
- Bridge as before: last warfarin Wed 5/10, enoxaparin 80 q12h from Fri 5/12, last dose AM 5/15. Restart post-op per surgeon, enoxaparin until INR >= 2.5, INR here a week after discharge.
- DM2: A1c today. Hold metformin AM of surgery.
- BP fine.
Cleared for surgery.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Right Hip Reimplantation
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 05/16/2023  Discharge 05/19/2023

Diagnosis: Treated periprosthetic joint infection, right hip, after first-stage resection and 6 weeks IV vancomycin.
Procedure 05/16/2023: Removal of antibiotic spacer and reimplantation of right total hip arthroplasty.

Operative findings: no purulence. Operative cultures: no growth at final read.

Course: Uncomplicated. Heparin bridge in hospital, warfarin restarted POD0; enoxaparin 80 mg q12h at discharge until INR >= 2.5 per PCP. Weight bearing as tolerated with walker. No antibiotics beyond routine perioperative prophylaxis.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge meds: home medications unchanged. Enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h until INR >= 2.5.
Disposition: home with home PT.
Follow-up: orthopedics 2 and 8 weeks; PCP for INR in 1 week.

events.reason: INR check after hip reimplantation, on enoxaparin bridge

documents.author: RN
documents.body:
1 wk after hip reimplantation. Walking with walker, doing home PT. Taking warfarin nightly and enoxaparin q12h. No bleeding.
INR in goal today. Per PCP: stop enoxaparin, continue warfarin 5 mg. Recheck 2 wks, then routine.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3 wks after R hip reimplantation. Relieved - says the hip feels 'like a hip again,' no ache, no fevers. Walking with a cane, PT twice a week. Appetite fine. No chest pain, no SOB at his current activity level. Bowels as usual (slow), stool softener a few times a week.

Meds unchanged. Warfarin back to routine.

Exam: BP and HR as charted. Regular, mechanical click. Lungs clear. R hip incision clean and healing, no erythema. Feet without lesions.

A/P:
1. DM2 - A1c in May was at his usual. Continue metformin.
2. HTN at goal.
3. Mechanical MVR - INR today, continue 5 mg.
4. CKD 3a - creatinine held steady through the vanc.
5. S/p two-stage R hip revision - ortho f/u in July.
6. Shingrix #2 today (a bit late, fine).
AWV in August.

documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY GROUP - CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 07/11/2023

8 weeks s/p second-stage reimplantation, right total hip, for chronic MRSE periprosthetic infection.

No hip pain. No fevers or sweats. Uses a cane outdoors only; none in the house. Done with formal PT.

Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: incision healed, no erythema, warmth or drainage. Painless ROM. Walks without a limp.
X-rays: well-seated components, no lucency.
Labs: ESR 18, CRP 2.8 mg/L.

Assessment: Periprosthetic infection treated; doing very well.
Plan: activity as tolerated, keep posterior hip precautions a few more weeks. Return 1 year with x-rays, sooner for pain, fever or wound change.

cc: PCP

documents.title: INR High
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
INR above goal today. Pt denies bleeding, bruising or dark stools. No new meds; admits he's been eating less (hot weather), no other change.
Per PCP: skip tonight's warfarin dose, then resume 5 mg nightly. Recheck 1 week. Pt repeated plan back.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Rough year with the hip, now behind him - walking without a cane in the house, short walks around the neighborhood. Mood good. PHQ-2 0. No falls this year. Independent with ADLs/IADLs, drives, manages his own meds with a weekly pill box and keeps his INR log. Hearing and vision fine (eye exam due - reminded).

Reviewed: problem list, meds, allergies (NKDA), family and social hx (former smoker, quit 2007, 20 pk-yr; 1-2 glasses wine/wk).

Exam: vitals as charted. Regular rhythm, mechanical click. Lungs clear. Abd benign. R hip healed. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable, skin intact.

Prevention:
- PCV20 today.
- Shingrix done x2.
- Flu/COVID this fall, RSV discussed - will do with the fall shots.
- Hep C screen today.
- AAA ultrasound ordered (ever-smoker, 65-75).
- Lung cancer screening: quit more than 15 yrs ago, not eligible.
- Colon: surveillance colonoscopy due ~spring 2024 (polyps 2021).
- Advance directive: he'll bring a copy.

Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UACR, INR.
RTC 3-4 months.

reports.text: Limited abdominal aortic ultrasound for aneurysm screening. The abdominal aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximum anteroposterior diameter 2.1 cm proximally, 1.8 cm distally. No focal dilatation. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber. No hydronephrosis incidentally noted.

documents.title: Aorta ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Graves - your aorta ultrasound was normal, no aneurysm. This is a one-time screening test, so nothing further needed. Your hepatitis C screen from August was negative too.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea on Exertion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since around late spring he gets winded on hills and the stairs up from his basement - noticed it more once he was walking again after the hip. Every so often lightheaded when he stands up or after exertion, passes in seconds. No chest pain, no palpitations, never passed out. No orthopnea, no leg swelling. No bleeding.

O: Vitals as charted. Regular rhythm, mechanical click present. There is a harsh systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border radiating up into both carotids - I don't have this documented before. Lungs clear. No edema. JVP not elevated.

A/P: Exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness with a harsh outflow-type systolic murmur in a man with a mechanical mitral valve - needs echo and cardiology. Referral placed with TTE, asked for a prompt slot. CBC/BMP today. Told him to stop and rest if lightheaded, no strenuous exertion until seen, ED for chest pain or fainting.

events.reason: Exertional dyspnea and dizziness; systolic murmur

conditions.label: Aortic valve stenosis
conditions.note: Severe: AVA 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 50 mmHg, LVEF 48%

reports.text:
Indication: dyspnea on exertion, systolic murmur, mechanical mitral valve.
Left ventricle: normal size. Mildly reduced systolic function, LVEF 48% by biplane Simpson. No regional wall motion abnormality.
Aortic valve: trileaflet, heavily calcified with restricted leaflet motion. Aortic valve area 0.8 cm2 by continuity. Mean gradient 50 mmHg. No significant aortic regurgitation.
Mitral valve: mechanical prosthesis, well seated, normal leaflet motion and normal transmitral gradient for prosthesis type; no paravalvular leak.
Right ventricle: normal size and function.
Atria: normal size.
Pericardium: no effusion.
IVC normal size with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Severe calcific aortic stenosis (AVA 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 50 mmHg). LVEF 48%. Normally functioning mechanical mitral prosthesis.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 11/17/2023
Referring: primary care

Reason: exertional dyspnea, occasional dizziness, systolic murmur.

HPI: 73-year-old man with a mechanical mitral valve (2013) on warfarin, managed by his PCP. For about six months he has had increasing breathlessness with exertion and occasional dizziness. He denies chest pain, palpitations and syncope.

PMH: mechanical MVR, HTN, DM2, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, chronic constipation, colon polyps, right hip arthroplasty with two-stage revision for infection in 2023.
Meds: warfarin 5 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker (20 pack-years, quit 2007), wine 1-2/week, retired teacher.
Family: no premature coronary disease.

Exam: BP 135/85, HR 78 regular. Harsh, late-peaking systolic murmur loudest at the right second intercostal space, radiating to the carotids. Crisp mechanical closing click. Lungs clear. No edema.

Echo today (report attached): severe calcific aortic stenosis - AVA 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 50 mmHg - with LVEF 48%. Mechanical mitral prosthesis functioning normally.

Assessment:
1. Severe aortic stenosis with exertional dyspnea and dizziness; LVEF 48%.
2. Mechanical mitral valve, normal prosthetic function; anticoagulation per PCP.
3. HTN, controlled.

Plan:
- He has a surveillance colonoscopy coming up for his history of polyps; that is scheduled.
- Continue current medicines without change.
- Warfarin and INR per PCP.
- Avoid heavy exertion; report syncope or chest pain immediately.

cc: PCP

documents.title: INR today
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Robert, your INR today is in range. Keep taking 5 mg every evening. Next check in about 5 weeks, before your colonoscopy - we'll go over the warfarin hold plan then.
